$comment: Explicit exceptions to the license policy enforced by scripts/check-licenses.mjs.
An entry here asserts that a person opened the package's actual LICENSE file and
read it. Nothing else counts: automated license detection reports 'other' /
NOASSERTION for projects whose LICENSE turns out to be the GNU GPL, so a machine
verdict alone can never justify an entry.
Entries are matched on name + version + declaredLicense, all exact. A version bump
ships a new artifact and a changed declaration means the terms moved — either one
retires the exception and requires a fresh reading. That is deliberate: the
Ask TWO questions, not one. 'Is it copyleft?' governs source disclosure. 'Is
redistribution granted?' governs whether we may ship it at all — a permissive-
sounding proprietary licence can grant use and stay silent on distribution, and
silence is not permission. Record the answer to both, and mark either one
'unresolved' rather than letting the copyleft answer stand in for both.
Never add an entry for a copyleft or source-available license (GPL, AGPL, LGPL,
SSPL, BUSL, Elastic). Those are disqualifying for the signed binaries we ship;
the dependency has to go instead.
Required fields: name, version, declaredLicense, reason.

packages.name: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk
packages.reason: Proprietary Anthropic terms, not copyleft. LICENSE.md reads in full: '(c) Anthropic PBC. All rights reserved. Use is subject to the Legal Agreements outlined here: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance.' The README section the manifest points at links the same Commercial Terms of Service. Grants use of the published package; imposes no source-disclosure obligation on wmux. Redistributed as an unmodified npm dependency. OPEN QUESTION — redistribution is not granted, only use. LICENSE.md reserves all rights; the linked Anthropic terms grant permission to USE the Services and are silent on redistributing, sublicensing or bundling SDK packages. wmux ships this package inside a signed installer, which is redistribution, not use. Read on 2026-07-28: no clause found either permitting or forbidding it. Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake this entry for a settled question. Not copyleft, so no source-disclosure obligation either way; the exposure is redistribution rights. Removing the package from the bundle and resolving it on the user's machine would retire the question entirely.
